version.changelog:
- Initial release of Playwright Stealth Scraper for OpenClaw.
- Enables scraping of dynamic websites with anti-bot defenses using Playwright and stealth plugins.
- Supports JavaScript-heavy sites including SPAs and React apps.
- Allows custom viewport and User-Agent spoofing.
- Provides the "stealth_scrape" tool for scraping by URL.

llm.summary: This skill is an unrestricted anti-bot web scraper, and its URL input can be abused to run local shell commands.

dimensions.detail: Arbitrary URL scraping with a full browser is high-impact network behavior, and the command-injection flaw can expand that authority to local command execution under the MCP server account.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package uses normal npm metadata and a lockfile, but package.json has caret dependency ranges, the lockfile confirms several vulnerable transitive dependencies, and the referenced scripts/playwright-stealth.js runtime file is absent from the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The MCP tool accepts a raw string URL and interpolates it into execSync, so a crafted URL can break out of the intended command; the input schema does not validate protocol, length, host, or shell metacharacters.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, credential harvesting, services, or memory writes were found, but exploitability of the shell command path would run attacker-chosen commands with the privileges and environment of the Node MCP process.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised scraping and stealth-browser behavior is coherent with the skill name and dependencies, but the tool targets any URL with bot-detection bypass and no authorization, rate-limit, or destination-scope guidance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only after the publisher replaces execSync string construction with an argument-array API, validates and restricts URLs, ships the missing scraper script, updates or pins dependencies, and documents that scraping must be limited to sites the user is authorized to access.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed in artifact/index.js: the user-controlled url is placed inside an execSync shell command. This is the main reason for Review.
[SQP-2] expected: Anti-bot scraping and stealth behavior are part of the stated purpose, but the artifacts provide no clear guardrails requiring authorized targets or responsible rate limits.
[SC4] unexpected: The lockfile confirms the dependency versions flagged by the scanner. These are supply-chain and availability risks, though less decisive than the command-injection issue.
[SC1] unexpected: The package.json dependency ranges are unpinned with caret specifiers; this is not malicious by itself, but it reduces install reproducibility for a powerful browser-automation skill.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only metadata and tool descriptions are present, but this is a usability/localization issue rather than evidence of hidden or malicious behavior.
